notes: Page 2 only shows the minifigure assembly (helmet, visor, head, torso, legs). None of these minifigure parts are in the supplied parts list or catalogue, so no pieces or joins were recorded for this page.
The parts list was provided, but this page has no quad bike building step.
Step 1 places the 2x6 plate b1 (first piece, rests_on []).

Step 2 turns b1 upside down and attaches two round 2x2 plates (b2, b3) to its underside: their studs clutch b1's anti-studs at the two ends. Which end each plate goes on, and the exact stud-to-anti-stud mapping, is read from the drawing.
The right-hand plate b3 is shown being added; the left-hand plate b2 is already in place.

Step 3 adds the two black wheel-holder plates (b4, b5) to the two round plates (b2, b3). The left one (b4) is already in place in the drawing and the right one (b5) is shown being added. I recorded both here, since the parts list has 2x lego-4600.
The assembly is upside down, so these joins are on the underside of the chassis plate b1. The wheel holder plates clutch the round plates' studs with their anti-studs.

That conflicts with the page 3 edges, which have the round plates' studs in b1's anti-studs. A round plate has studs on one face only, so the earlier stud/anti-stud direction for b2 and b3 may be wrong. The adjacency is the same either way: b4 and b5 sit on b2 and b3, which sit on b1.

Step 4 shows the chassis flipped over, with the wheel-holder plates underneath. At each end of the 2x6 plate b1 a dark side-handle plate (2540) sits in the outermost column and a light 1x2 plate (3023) sits in the next column. The handles stick out past the ends of the chassis.
The drawing shows the finished step, with no arrows. I inferred which plate goes where from stud colours.
Each 1x2 plate lies across the width of b1, covering one column of two studs. The stud mapping is inferred.

Step 5 adds two orange mudguards, one on each end of the chassis. The left one (b10) is already in place in the drawing and the right one (b11) is shown being added. Each covers the 2x2 stud area of the side-handle plate and 1x2 plate at that end.
The mudguard's centre 2x2 anti-studs (columns 2 and 3 of its 2x4 footprint) clutch those studs. The exact anti-stud mapping is inferred.
The side handles (b6, b8) stay visible at the outer ends.

Step 6 covers the mudguards. The right mudguard (b11) gets a white grille tile (b12) on its inner two studs, already in place in the drawing, and a white jumper plate (b13), shown being added, on its outer two studs. The left mudguard (b10) already has two white jumper plates (b14, b15) side by side covering its 2x2 studs.
The drawing shows the left jumpers already placed with no arrows. I counted 3 jumpers and 1 grille against the parts list, which matches.
Each jumper is 1x2 and covers two studs but has only one stud on top. Which stud columns each piece covers is inferred from the picture.

Step 7 has no arrows. I inferred it from the finished drawing. A trans-yellow cheese slope (the headlight, b16) sits on the outer jumper plate b14 on the left mudguard. A dark gray clip tile (b17) sits on the inner jumper plate b15.
Which of the two jumper studs each piece sits on is inferred from their positions in the drawing.

Step 8 has three parts. The handlebars (b18) clip into the clip tile b17 on the left end (the front, with the headlight slope). The antenna (b19) goes on the stud of the white jumper b13 on the right mudguard. The blue flag (b20) is first clipped onto the antenna shaft, shown in the inset.
The antenna has no port for the clipped flag, so that edge has no v_port. The flag's two clips grip the shaft.
The handlebars join the clip by pin/clip, with rotation about the clip axis.

Step 9 builds four wheels. Each is a white wheel pushed into a black tyre (inset), and each is then fitted on a wheel-holder pin of b4 or b5, two per holder plate. The 4 tyres and 4 wheels match the parts list.
I used the 4600's axle-hole.1 and axle-hole.2 ports for the holder pins. The pins sit on opposite sides of each holder plate, so the wheel-to-port mapping is arbitrary.

The minifigure, which was built on page 2, is placed on the finished quad bike. Its parts are not in the parts list or catalogue, so I left it out. The finished picture shows the rider seated between the handlebars and the flag.
Page 11 is the parts inventory with customer service info. It has no building step, so nothing was added.
Page 12 is an advertisement for other LEGO City Coast Guard sets (7737, 7738, 7739). It has no building step, so nothing was added.
Page 13 is an advertisement for LEGO City Police sets. It has no building step, so nothing was added.
Page 14 is the LEGO Club membership form. It has no building step, so nothing was added.
Page 15 is a LEGO Club and LEGO Shop advertisement. It has no building step, so nothing was added.
Page 16 is a promotional back cover with a competition notice. It has no building step, so nothing was added.
